body: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative n-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor p(x_n x1:n-1) through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. n controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter d controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing n-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controlled approximations by using tree-grams as generative models. In particular, we show that hyperparameter transfer under μP can be made more robust when narrower models are tuned on simpler data, generated by tree-grams with moderate n and d. In addition, we show that entropy and effective range of correlations control performance gap after fine-tuning. This is because tree-grams allow us to explicitly control horizon and capacity. When allowed to route across candidate topologies, we observe emergent sparsity in tree-grams. Such concentrated routing permits pruning upto 95% of topologies without significant change in performance.
